subject: Midday latency surge — coordination, product asks, and customer readout
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Patel <lina@nimblecartpro.com>, ops@nimblecartpro.com
Date: 2026-10-01T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Midday latency surge — initial sync and customer comms

Team —

We started seeing a p95/p99 latency jump for NimbleCartPro at ~11:48 PT (spike lasted ~14m, then partial stabilization). Lina (cc'd) flagged increased timeouts in their checkout flow. High-level ask: rapid triage, surface product tradeoffs (routing/rolling back recent runtime changes), and a short external readout we can send to NimbleCartPro within the hour.

Immediate questions:
- Ben/Karthik: what does initial telemetry show as the likely source? kernel change, cache evaporation, routing?
- Marissa: if we need to apply a temporary product-level mitigation (e.g., force-prefetch, fallback to smaller model, or temporary throttles), what impacts on quality/cost do we expect?
- CS (Lina): What are the customer-visible failures and their tolerance for a short mitigation?

Suggested quick plan (please confirm or amend):
1) SRE triage + short RCA (10–20m).
2) If root cause is recent runtime change, consider rolling that back to reduce latency window.
3) If capacity/routing related, apply a targeted routing override for nimblecartpro traffic and enable aggressive prefix caching.
4) Draft a 3–4 line customer readout; attach to thread for review.

Attachments: latency_graph_20261001.png (latest 30m window) — will update with raw traces.

Thanks — Hannah
--
Hannah Schmitt
Account Manager, Large Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Patel <lina@nimblecartpro.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T12:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Midday latency surge — initial sync and customer comms

On Thu, 2026-10-01 at 12:05, Hannah Schmitt wrote:
> We started seeing a p95/p99 latency jump for NimbleCartPro at ~11:48 PT...

Quick triage summary (12:17 PT):
- Observed a ~3–5x jump in p95 and ~6x in p99 for their gen-api endpoint between 11:48–12:02 PT. Token throughput held, error rate modestly increased (~0.8%).
- Correlated signal: elevated KV-cache miss rate on the pool serving NimbleCartPro (cache size saw a transient eviction spike).
- Recent change: a kernel scheduling tweak (PR #NCP-4591) rolled out to the autoscaler pool at 11:30 PT — timeline matches.
- Hypothesis: increased contention from the kernel change plus a fanout pattern from a burst of long-context requests caused KV cache churn and jitter in tail latencies.

Immediate mitigation options (pros/cons):
A) Roll back PR NCP-4591 to the previous kernel scheduling parameters — likely to reduce tail latency quickly; risk: slight throughput flicker during rollback.
B) Apply a routing override to shift NimbleCartPro traffic to a warmed dedicated pool (if capacity exists) — lower risk to other customers, but requires capacity and may take ~5–10m to re-route.
C) Enable conservative prefix/KV prefetching and reduce concurrent streaming windows for their route — mitigates tail but increases token cost.

Next steps I recommend: roll back NCP-4591 now (we can target rolling rollback to a subset of instances to reduce blast radius) while we prepare a routing override if rollback isn't sufficient. I'll open/updated Jira NCP-4591 with traces.

Ben
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T12:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Midday latency surge — initial sync and customer comms

Ben — thanks for the quick triage. A few notes from the runtime side: we pushed a micro-optimization to kernel sharding (NCP-4591) to reduce overall CPU scheduling overhead; it appears to have interacted poorly with long-context loads that NimbleCartPro started sending this morning.

I can do a targeted rollback on the autoscaler pool now (command below) and monitor KV hit/miss and p99. If rollback doesn't bring p99 down in 8–10m, we'll open the routing override to move their route to a warmed pool.

Rollback plan (15m):
- Execute: deploy rollback tag kernel-shard-v2 -> kernel-shard-v1 on pool-autoscale-03 (target 30% instances first).
- Watch: p50/p95/p99 + KV hit rate + streaming latencies.
- If stable after subset rollback, continue phased rollback.

Tradeoffs: rollback should reduce tail latency with minimal impact to throughput; if we instead choose routing override + prefix prefetch, we'll likely increase cost ~8–12% for NimbleCartPro until we stabilize.

I'll proceed with the phased rollback unless anyone objects.

Karthik
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Lina Patel <lina@nimblecartpro.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@nimblecartpro.com, Anthony Wu <aw@nimblecartpro.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Midday latency surge — initial sync and customer comms

Thanks for the fast responses. Visible impact on our side: elevated checkout latency, a small uptick in abandoned carts (non-critical but trending). We can tolerate a short mitigation (10–60m) as long as there is a clear rollback plan and we get a short customer-facing note we can share internally.

Two asks from us:
1) If rollback is low-risk and expected to help, please proceed. We prefer rollback over temporary throttles that might reduce throughput.
2) If you expect route-level fallback (e.g., to a smaller model), confirm quality implications. We can accept that for 30–60m if it eliminates timeouts.

Please keep us posted on ETA to a stable state. Lina
Director, Platform Engineering
NimbleCartPro
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Patel <lina@nimblecartpro.com>, ops@nimblecartpro.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Customer readout (draft) — midday latency surge 10/01

Lina / NimbleCartPro team —

Thanks again for flagging the issue this morning. Quick readout (we'll push this to you once Ben/Karthik confirm the final state):

What happened: between ~11:48–12:02 PT we observed an increase in tail latency impacting a subset of NimbleCartPro traffic. Initial root cause was a kernel scheduling change that interacted with a burst of long-context requests causing elevated KV-cache eviction and tail jitter.

What we did: our engineers immediately performed a phased rollback of the kernel scheduling change and monitored latency and cache metrics; we also prepared a routing override to shift traffic to a warmed pool if rollback did not fully resolve the spike.

Current status: rollback has been applied to the autoscaler subset and preliminary metrics show p95 improving; Ben/Karthik are continuing monitoring and will confirm when we reach full stabilization.

Next steps:
- We'll confirm stabilization within the hour and share final traces.
- Postmortem with corrective actions (including a safer rollout pattern for NCP-4591 and additional KV-cache safeguards) to follow in 48–72 hours.

If this draft looks good, we'll send as an outbound note to your ops channel and include the latency_graph_20261001.png and the full trace link.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Manager, Large Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: customer_readout_draft.docx
